body:
Easily accessible drop boxes, clarifying the tricky witness signature requirement, more time to cure valid ballots with tiny errors so that they count instead of getting thrown out... this Wisconsin Supreme Court ruling helps increase ballot access, making it easier to vote and improving voter participation.
Supporting private lawsuits like this one in Wisconsin around the rest of the country will make every voice heard in our elections. RUSH $25 or more right now to help protect and expand the right to vote >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=101324_3&amount=25]
Voter Action Project Logo [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-weekly?refcode=101324_3&amount=25]
Kenosha News: Wisconsin Supreme Court reverses previous decision, allows absentee ballot drop boxes [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=101324_3&amount=25]
To quote the president, Team: This "is a big f-ing deal".
The Wisconsin Supreme Court made a key pro-voter ruling and reversed its previous two-year-old decision banning absentee ballot drop boxes . This current, liberal-controlled court made the change from the previous, conservative high court, which banned drop boxes in a highly politicized decision after pressure from opponents of voting rights.
Essentially, the 4-3 ruling means that freestanding, mailbox-like drop boxes — which Wisconsin used effectively, safely, and securely in previous elections — can again be used to collect absentee ballots this fall.
Wisconsin's elected officials are thrilled and ready to comply: “ Allowing eligible voters an accessible and secure way to cast a ballot just makes sense ,” Madison Mayor Satya Rhodes-Conway said. She added that “ Madison is ready to follow the law and promote democracy .”
Team: This decision shows how we can win in our fight to defend access to the ballot and increase voter participation across this country. These 64 Democracy Defenders — from races in Arizona, Michigan, Minnesota, New Hampshire, and Wisconsin — are dedicated to protecting the fundamental rights of the American people:
* **In Arizona** , Republicans hold just a two-seat majority in both the State House and Senate. If we can help get out the vote and win a majority in both chambers, we can build power that can be used to strengthen the state’s redistricting process.
* **In Michigan** , we have the opportunity to help Democrats keep their trifecta, which will protect the state’s redistricting reform and allow for more landmark policies to protect the freedoms of Michiganders statewide.
* **In Minnesota** , we’re also working to protect this state’s Democratic trifecta. A single special election will determine control of the Minnesota State Senate, and Republicans only need to flip five seats in the House to regain power here.
* **In New Hampshire** , Republicans have a trifecta, but we have a real chance to flip that on its head. Not only can we win majorities in the legislature, where Republicans are defending tiny majorities —**now, we’re adding the governor’s race to our priority list!** The state House is rated a toss-up and the Senate is considered to be within reach. body:
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2059%2E135344%2EHaUaue)

Friend --
In just 23 days, it will be Election Day.
With your permission, I’d appreciate the chance to make the case for why a donation to my campaign for U.S. Senate before that happens is one of the most strategic contributions you can make today.
Let me start with what you probably already instinctively know: Michigan is going to be a critical state for the 2024 campaign.
There is no winning the White House without Michigan. For Democrats, there is no holding the Senate without Michigan. Even our House delegation rests on a one-seat Democratic majority.
But you were probably already sold on the importance of Michigan. So, aside from the fact that control of the U.S. Senate is at stake (!), what about my race? Why donate to my campaign?
This is one of the rare open Senate races without an incumbent running -- in fact, it’s one of the few competitive races in the entire country. That means we have A LOT of introducing of me to do across the state.
Reaching those folks takes resources, and that's not something I can do without you.
Add the fact that this is going to be one of the most expensive races in the country -- not just with candidate spending, but outside spending too.
And I'll close with the news that in all of my elections, I have historically done better than Democrats usually do in the "redder" areas of the state. That means I am finding and pulling voters other races couldn't, and that is good for Kamala Harris and every other Democrat on the ballot on Election Day.
So yes, this race is kind of a unicorn. It's a unique situation where control of the White House and Congress is on the line, most voters don't know the candidates yet, and the Democratic Senate candidate can help the top of the ticket.
[**That's why I am asking for your support: Can I count on you to make a contribution to my campaign for U.S. Senate before our final FEC deadline ends in a few days? clean_body: Friend -- In just 23 days, it will be Election Day. With your permission, I’d appreciate the chance to make the case for why a donation to my campaign for U.S. Senate before that happens is one of the most strategic contributions you can make today. Let me start with what you probably already instinctively know: Michigan is going to be a critical state for the 2024 campaign. There is no winning the White House without Michigan. For Democrats, there is no holding the Senate without Michigan. Even our House delegation rests on a one-seat Democratic majority. But you were probably already sold on the importance of Michigan. So, aside from the fact that control of the U.S. Senate is at stake (!), what about my race? Why donate to my campaign? This is one of the rare open Senate races without an incumbent running -- in fact, it’s one of the few competitive races in the entire country. That means we have A LOT of introducing of me to do across the state. Reaching those folks takes resources, and that's not something I can do without you. Add the fact that this is going to be one of the most expensive races in the country -- not just with candidate spending, but outside spending too. And I'll close with the news that in all of my elections, I have historically done better than Democrats usually do in the "redder" areas of the state. That means I am finding and pulling voters other races couldn't, and that is good for Kamala Harris and every other Democrat on the ballot on Election Day. So yes, this race is kind of a unicorn. It's a unique situation where control of the White House and Congress is on the line, most voters don't know the candidates yet, and the Democratic Senate candidate can help the top of the ticket. | **ABOUT NELLA**
**New Mexico is Nella Domenici’s home. She was born in Albuquerque and lived for most of her childhood in a home near the intersection of Lomas and Monroe with her seven siblings, and her parents - Pete and Nancy Domenici. Nella began her education at Our Lady of Fatima, where she learned the values she holds today. Nella is a proud third-generation New Mexican, devoted mother of two, step-mom of four, and the wife of a Navy Veteran. Nella’s family’s roots run deep in New Mexico and she and her husband Pat enjoy their family home in New Mexico that they have owned for nearly twenty years.

Like most New Mexicans, Nella Domenici understands the importance of hard work. She waited tables to help pay for her undergraduate degree from Georgetown University, and worked her way through night school at Georgetown Law while holding down a full time job. She then graduated from Harvard Business School as a Baker Scholar, top 5% of the class, while 9 months pregnant.

Nella began her career at the bottom and worked her way up through the complex finance world, eventually serving as CFO for one of the world’s largest, most successful investment firms. In her career, Nella advised, invested in, grew, and led many companies, and served on public company boards. The industries she has worked in are vast and include areas such as health care, AI, food service, lodging, commercial real estate, mortgage lending, and consumer products. These companies have ranged from small family-owned businesses, to rapidly growing venture backed enterprises, to a Fortune 200 company. Several of these have been headquartered in New Mexico. Collectively, the companies Nella has been heavily involved with have employed thousands of Americans.

Like her father and mother, Nella has been a warrior for those who most need an advocate: for women competing in academics or business, for families dealing with mental illness, and for those without access to quality healthcare or education. **

Inside Trump’s Aurora Rally: Bold Plans, Big Energy, and Colorado’s Call for Change
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s2maa8953e8)
---
**October 13, 2024** **SUNDAY NEWS DIGEST** **By Heidi Ganahl**
| | Dear Rocky Mountain Voice Readers,
This past Friday, I had the chance to attend the highly anticipated MAGA rally in Aurora at the Gaylord Rockies Resort & Convention Center with my whole family, and what an unforgettable, one-in-a-lifetime experience to share together! Thousands of Coloradans showed up early, eager to secure their spots and hear former President Trump share his vision for the future of our country. The energy was palpable, as supporters lined up even before dawn, determined to be part of this moment in our state’s history.
The rally, packed with a sea of red hats and flags, was a clear message to both the political establishment and the media: Coloradans are ready to stand up for their beliefs and values. Trump addressed the crowd with his signature energy, discussing everything from border security to economic recovery and public safety. He pledged a national initiative called “Operation Aurora,” promising to crack down on illegal immigration and restore law and order in our communities, using Aurora as a model for his future plans.
Governor Jared Polis and some leading Democratic lawmakers attempted to grandstand and distract from the event, planning their own counter-messaging. However, it was a flop with only a handful of people in attendance. The stark difference in the two events made it clear that Trump’s message is resonating deeply with the people of Colorado, eager to hear solutions to the growing concerns we face as a state and nation.
Trump’s emphasis on making America safe again was a central theme, with his policies aimed at strengthening law enforcement, revitalizing the economy, and securing our borders. As we look ahead to the 2024 election, it’s clear that the movement supporting Trump is stronger than ever in Colorado. Friday’s rally was not just a moment of excitement but a reminder that many are ready to push back against policies that have left our communities vulnerable and our voices unheard.
**Check out the following articles for a deeper dive on Trump's visit:**
* **[In MAGA rally, Trump pledges national ‘Operation Aurora’ to address illegal aliens](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/sdib599013d)**
* **[Thousands of Coloradans didn’t sleep in to guarantee place in MAGA rally at Gaylord in Aurora](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s7re931eed1)**
* **[At MAGA rally in Aurora, Coloradans will hear Trump policies to ‘make America safe again’](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s9iadfbf1f6)**
* **[Gov. Polis, leading Democrat lawmakers plan to grandstand Trump’s MAGA rally](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/sfi18a22887)**

Thank you to all who made it out to the rally! Let’s keep the momentum going and continue to fight for the future of our state and country.
In liberty, Heidi Ganahl

**[Ganahl: Remembering our friend, inspiration and Rocky Mountain Voice champion Buz Koelbel](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/sat5bc3f86a)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s1ifbb0c106) Buz Koelbel was a force of nature — a builder of legacies, a man of unwavering principles and a guiding light for all who had the privilege of knowing him.
**[‘High energy’ Trump to kickoff whirlwind sprint through four states in three days with Aurora](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s3s25597e3e)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/sfud8c08983) It might be said former President Donald J. Trump is proving to be “high energy”, as he sometimes will describe a go-getter on the campaign trail.
**[A view from both sides of the 29 Road Interchange ballot measure in Mesa County](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/sdn939d7870)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s6qbf1558d4) For decades, Mesa County folks have been dreaming of a common sense road fix to link 29 Road straight to Interstate 70. That connection is almost a reality.

**STATE**
**[How to register to vote, cast your ballot and more FAQs about Colorado’s 2024 election](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s4vd8e3a4a9)** [THE COLORADO SUN](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/sdi3af3bacc) Election day is Nov. 5, and voters across Colorado will be casting ballots that will decide the outcome of the presidential race, congressional contests, statewide ballot measures, legislative battles and a myriad of local issues.
**[Oil& gas debate unveils tension between industry, environmental protection interests](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s0l70539cf3)** [COLORADO POLITICS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s0haca76b0a) The wide divide between oil and gas development and environmental protection was on full display as a conservation organization representative debated one from the Colorado Oil and Gas Association.

**[U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson says one Colorado race could help decide control of Congress](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s8m26d9a414)** [CBS COLORADO](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/sfu96eeba30) In a sign of how competitive the race in Colorado’s 8th Congressional District is, U.S. Speaker of the House Mike Johnson made his second visit to the district in seven weeks to raise money and support for Republican Gabe Evans.
_**[READ MORE STATE NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/sfn081b040c)**_

**NATIONAL**
**[CO Gov., Harris Surrogate: She Just Had Hard Time Thinking of Differences from Biden ‘on the Spot’](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s5kd05f44d9)** [BREITBART](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s9v4aa21137) On Friday’s broadcast of CNN’s “The Source,” Colorado Gov. Jared Polis (D), who is also a Harris-Walz Surrogate, said that 2024 Democratic presidential candidate Vice President Kamala Harris “is a totally different person” from President Joe Biden, but she didn’t mention what she would have done differently because “it’s hard to think of things on the spot.”
**[Trump, Harris locked in dead heat in 7 battleground states, poll finds: ‘Could not be closer’](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s1k146dad04)** [FOX NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s5n23a5544a) A new Wall Street Journal poll has found little separation between former President Trump and Vice President Kamala Harris in seven battleground states, prompting a Democratic pollster to say that the 2024 election “really could not be closer.”
**[DeSantis rips Harris again for butting into Milton response: ‘No role in this process’](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s8j655c1c9d)** [NEW YORK POST](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/sam6d51c731) Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis briefed President Biden on the fallout from Hurricane Milton Thursday morning while hammering Vice President Kamala Harris once again over her swipe at him for not taking her call earlier this week.
**[Biden-Harris Administration has no clue how many unvetted aliens it let in](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/sek741c9653)** [THE FEDERALIST](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/sbu6fd12fa0) The inspector general of the Department of Homeland Security issued a new report revealing that the Biden-Harris administration has endangered Americans’ safety by intentionally welcoming millions of illegal immigrants into the U.S. without properly vetting them.
**[Tim Walz calls for elimination of Electoral College at California fundraiser, says ‘it needs to go’](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/sao7e32586d)** [FOX NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/sfme6278fc5) Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz on Tuesday called for the elimination of the Electoral College during a fundraiser in California, a move some Democrats have advocated for in the past after election defeats.
**[READ MORE NATIONAL NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/sdu1dc442f3)**
|

**LOCAL**
**[U.S. Rep. Lauren Boebert listens to Western Slope leaders on energy, water and land use](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s9j34858668)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/sap72b05227) Meet Bryce and Lisa Casto, sixth-generation ranchers on the Western Slope, who are worried that the Dolores Monument designation will close their roads and leave them unable to care for their livestock.
**[Grand Junction still seeking answers to homeless issue, following drug arrests at resource center](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/sau840b3e6a)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s9ta69bb63f) When the Grand Junction City Council was forming their plan in 2023 to find temporary shelters for the approximately 2,300 homeless people who were living in the streets, members of the community had multiple concerns about the potential problems with the proposed housing.
**[School board leaders in Southern Colorado campaign against local marijuana measures](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s9m74c89042)** [COLORADO SPRINGS GAZETTE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s5me1a51d10) Elected officials from across the Colorado Springs region are lending their voices to a campaign opposing recreational marijuana sales in the city.
**[Denver’s 7A: What you need to know about RTD’s request to keep all its sales tax revenue](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s9t50cab57f)** [THE COLORADO SUN](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s6rdab9b840) Metro Denver-area voters will decide Nov. 5 whether the Regional Transportation District can continue to keep all of its sales tax revenue in coming years, even when a strong economy pushes revenue up above caps set in the Taxpayer’s Bill of Rights.
**_[READ MORE LOCAL NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s6gef8ec323)_**
|

**COMMENTARY**
**[Chandler: Vote ‘no’ on Arapahoe County ballot issue 1A](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s7m2165345d)** [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s0l2335c4ab) _Our Taxpayer Bill of Rights (TABOR) is under perpetual attack by a government that seeks to grow without the consent of the governed. A major tenant of TABOR is asking our permission to raise our taxes. That is all we ask. Government, make your case. Why do you need more tax revenue?_ __
**[Caldara: Taxpayers subsidize Progressive war on affordable energy](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/sckc791686f)** [COMPLETE COLORADO](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s5u0362fbf1) _“350 Colorado” is an anti-fossil fuels organization which lobbies to end the state’s oil and gas industry. They organize anti-energy zealots to march, protest and pressure lawmakers. Proud of their role in civil disobedience during Colorado Oil and Gas Commission hearings, they take credit for helping pass the “strictest anti-fracking regulations in the state.” Blah, blah, blah._
**[Grabar: Kamala Harris is poised to revive the worst aspects of FDR’s socialist agenda](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s2o51152ebb)** [THE FEDERALIST](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.-g/s1r3a305fa0) _At the Economic Club of Pittsburgh, Democratic presidential candidate Kamala Harris recently said she would “engage in what Franklin Roosevelt called ‘bold, persistent experimentation,’” as he had told the 1932 graduating class at Oglethorpe University. But she did not mention FDR’s vision of “remaking the world,” which included fundamentally changing “our popular economic thought” to see to “a wiser, more equitable distribution of the national income.”_

Governor Jared Polis and some leading Democratic lawmakers attempted to grandstand and distract from the event, planning their own counter-messaging. However, it was a flop with only a handful of people in attendance. The stark difference in the two events made it clear that Trump’s message is resonating deeply with the people of Colorado, eager to hear solutions to the growing concerns we face as a state and nation. Trump’s emphasis on making America safe again was a central theme, with his policies aimed at strengthening law enforcement, revitalizing the economy, and securing our borders. As we look ahead to the 2024 election, it’s clear that the movement supporting Trump is stronger than ever in Colorado. Friday’s rally was not just a moment of excitement but a reminder that many are ready to push back against policies that have left our communities vulnerable and our voices unheard. Check out the following articles for a deeper dive on Trump's visit: Thank you to all who made it out to the rally! Let’s keep the momentum going and continue to fight for the future of our state and country. In liberty, Heidi Ganahl | | | TOP STORIES OF THE WEEK All of the voter resources available to English-language speakers and readers are also available to Spanish-language speakers and readers in Colorado through VayaVotarColorado.gov, the office of Secretary of State Jena Griswold has announced. Buz Koelbel was a force of nature — a builder of legacies, a man of unwavering principles and a guiding light for all who had the privilege of knowing him. It might be said former President Donald J. Trump is proving to be “high energy”, as he sometimes will describe a go-getter on the campaign trail. For decades, Mesa County folks have been dreaming of a common sense road fix to link 29 Road straight to Interstate 70. That connection is almost a reality. | STATE Election day is Nov. 5, and voters across Colorado will be casting ballots that will decide the outcome of the presidential race, congressional contests, statewide ballot measures, legislative battles and a myriad of local issues. The wide divide between oil and gas development and environmental protection was on full display as a conservation organization representative debated one from the Colorado Oil and Gas Association. The Colorado Supreme Court, by 4-3, declined on Tuesday to address the high-profile issue of a Christian baker’s refusal to make a cake for a customer celebrating a gender transition, instead concluding the case was not properly filed in the first place. In a sign of how competitive the race in Colorado’s 8th Congressional District is, U.S. Speaker of the House Mike Johnson made his second visit to the district in seven weeks to raise money and support for Republican Gabe Evans. | NATIONAL On Friday’s broadcast of CNN’s “The Source,” Colorado Gov. Jared Polis (D), who is also a Harris-Walz Surrogate, said that 2024 Democratic presidential candidate Vice President Kamala Harris “is a totally different person” from President Joe Biden, but she didn’t mention what she would have done differently because “it’s hard to think of things on the spot.” A new Wall Street Journal poll has found little separation between former President Trump and Vice President Kamala Harris in seven battleground states, prompting a Democratic pollster to say that the 2024 election “really could not be closer.” Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis briefed President Biden on the fallout from Hurricane Milton Thursday morning while hammering Vice President Kamala Harris once again over her swipe at him for not taking her call earlier this week. The inspector general of the Department of Homeland Security issued a new report revealing that the Biden-Harris administration has endangered Americans’ safety by intentionally welcoming millions of illegal immigrants into the U.S. without properly vetting them. Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz on Tuesday called for the elimination of the Electoral College during a fundraiser in California, a move some Democrats have advocated for in the past after election defeats. | LOCAL Meet Bryce and Lisa Casto, sixth-generation ranchers on the Western Slope, who are worried that the Dolores Monument designation will close their roads and leave them unable to care for their livestock. When the Grand Junction City Council was forming their plan in 2023 to find temporary shelters for the approximately 2,300 homeless people who were living in the streets, members of the community had multiple concerns about the potential problems with the proposed housing. Elected officials from across the Colorado Springs region are lending their voices to a campaign opposing recreational marijuana sales in the city. Metro Denver-area voters will decide Nov. 5 whether the Regional Transportation District can continue to keep all of its sales tax revenue in coming years, even when a strong economy pushes revenue up above caps set in the Taxpayer’s Bill of Rights. | COMMENTARY Our Taxpayer Bill of Rights (TABOR) is under perpetual attack by a government that seeks to grow without the consent of the governed. A major tenant of TABOR is asking our permission to raise our taxes. That is all we ask. Government, make your case. Why do you need more tax revenue? “350 Colorado” is an anti-fossil fuels organization which lobbies to end the state’s oil and gas industry. They organize anti-energy zealots to march, protest and pressure lawmakers. Proud of their role in civil disobedience during Colorado Oil and Gas Commission hearings, they take credit for helping pass the “strictest anti-fracking regulations in the state.” Blah, blah, blah. #
Peter — is there anything at all I can say to encourage you to add your first donation of any amount toward our grassroots campaign to elect Lucas Kunce during the final stretch of this election?
**We’ve got 23 days left until Election Day, and early voting starts in just 9 days.**
**[DEFEAT JOSH HAWLEY: CHIP IN NOW →](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/76181?refcode=em20241013-8044&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=8044%2E614464%2EiEkBa8)**

**Your support helps our campaign expose Josh Hawley as the control-obsessed politician he really is, and it helps us fight back against the attacks that are already being thrown at Lucas and our movement.**

**Knock Knock - Reports from Canvassing**
In New York 21, I'm happy to report that there is a silent majority of voters who seem to have a plan to vote blue this November.
My polling is not scientific. It is not tested. It is not statistically measured for accuracy.
My polling is based on dropping in on three different random blocks in three different cities, each chosen for the convenience en route to another destination.
In Massena (St. Lawrence County), we picked a block that appeared to be populated by the working poor. I'm basing this on the condition of the homes. It was a block that had a mixture of manufactured homes, apartments, duplexes, and single-family homes. All of them seemed like the last stop before doubling up with a cousin or being out on the street. Again - this wasn't scientific data-gathering. This is purely anecdotal.
Out of 28 homes, we met someone just waking up at noon from an all-night shift at a hospital. She was cool, really glad that someone from my campaign stopped by, and apologetic that we were seeing her in jammies and before her cup of morning coffee. We met 5 stay-at-home moms. A few were supporters. Another said she was not registered to vote; they were "thinking" about it,. One person angrily said she couldn't see the point of voting.
Curiously, for a Friday morning when school should be in session, we saw a number of kids riding bicycles or playing in the yards. (The Special Education teacher in me wanted to ask why they weren't in school, but I refrained.) We met 2 people as they were walking their dogs. We met one guy who seemed to emerge from a cave, shocked that anybody was knocking on his door. He said he was not a voter. I met someone who had an Elise Stefanik sign in her garage that she just had not put out. She said she was thinking. We chatted. I have no idea if I persuaded her or not.
In Malone (Franklin County), we picked a street that seemed a little more stable socio-economically, based on the condition of the homes, all of which were single-family residences. (Maybe I'm wrong and they are just a lot deeper in debt than the Massena neighborhood.) Mostly we had positive reactions. "Oh yeah -- ya got my vote!"
We met a veteran who was also a retired law enforcement officer. He was angry. His wife had lost 6 cousins in the hurricane North Carolina, and he wanted to know why we were supporting migrants crossing the border illegally, instead of helping our own American citizens. I took a deep breath, and quietly said that I'm sure in his professional experience, he knew a lot about government budgets. There just wasn't any easy way to divert millions of dollars from one line item in the budget to another. I reminded him that Trump had done it; Biden had not. He calmed down. My staffer said, "I see your thin blue line flag. He said yes. We talked about how police officers had been beaten on January 6 and my opponent defends those who participated in the attack. I said bluntly: "She doesn't back the police. She backs Trump." He nodded, looked down, and said, "Yeah." Later I saw him in the neighborhood walking his dog. We smiled and were friendly. Maybe I had a little bit of influence? Hard to say.
Honestly, most of the doors we knocked on in Malone were really glad to see us, and they proudly assured us that I had their vote.
In Plattsburgh (Clinton County) we picked a block that seemed to have upper-middle-class homes. Again - appearances only. I did not check the property tax rolls. House after house was positive. "You're running against Elise? Ya got my vote!" We even heard that through a ring camera from someone who wasn't home. Two notable exceptions: a person who was friendly at first, but then when he asked my party affiliation, I lost him. We were still friendly. But the conversation chilled at that point. Another group of three young African American men seemed non-committal. One said he would not vote because he doesn't see the point. The other two weren't sure what their voting plan was.
Here's my point: nobody slammed a door in my face. Nobody said, "Get the (bleep) off-a my porch!" Definitely no weapons were wielded. And these were random stops -- no VAN data, no idea who these people were or what their prior voting record might be.
I could canvass like this all day every day. One of my favorite aspects of running for office is talking to undecided voters. They keep me alert, and offer me a challenge.
**Can we talk about the protections against age discrimination in NY Prop 1?**
NY Proposition 1 "adds certain protections to the State Bill of Rights."
"Adds anti-discrimination provisions to State Constitution. Covers ethnicity, national origin, age, disability, and sex, including sexual orientation, gender identity and pregnancy. Also covers reproductive healthcare and autonomy. A "YES" vote puts these protections against discrimination in the New York State Constitution. A "NO" vote leaves these protections out of the State Constitution."
The disinformation wars are rampant. The naysayers predict that if NY Prop 1 passes boy children will join girls' sports teams and invade their locker rooms. They will also go to school as one gender and come home having had gender reassignment surgery.
I guess they've never gotten a call from the school nurse demanding that their feverish child be picked up immediately. Schools can't even give a kid a Tylenol to keep a fever down, much less perform gender reassignment surgery.
The other piece of misinformation from the naysayers is that illegal immigrants will be allowed to vote in our elections. Not true.
I'm all for writing any protections possible into the State Constitution. No new law will be made by passing Prop 1. We just want to keep the protections we have.
I realize that a lot of the discussion in favor of Prop 1 has centered on reproductive and gender-affirming choice.
I really think that for a certain kind of voter we need to focus on the protections against age discrimination. Maybe you have known someone older than 50 who mysteriously experiences out-of-the-blue harassment at work, only to realize that the employer is trying to perhaps encourage them to quit in order to hire someone half as old at half the salary. Or perhaps you've spoken with someone who has actually been downsized or laid off, only to realize they can't even get an interview, much less a job. Prop 1 and its protections against age discrimination are necessary. Yes, we have protections against age discrimination in the Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967. New York has a similar law. But these are really tough cases to prove. Let's codify these protections, so they are less likely to be repealed if we should ever get another MAGA administration.

**Champy is here. Where is Elise?**
My team has very cleverly introduced a campaign mascot to our social media presence. In Lake Champlain, there is a Loch Ness sort of legendary creature that dates back to 1609. My team now takes a small Democratic Blue dinosaur with us, and caption a photo with something like, "Champy is here. Where is Elise?"
On Saturday week we attended the dedication of the Raquette Lake Fire Department. For starters, it's a gorgeous facility. It will allow the fire department to park state-of-the-art fire trucks (the old facility was too small for modern fire trucks). There is ample space to move around the vehicles so that proper training of new volunteer firefighters can take place. And there is ample space to park ambulances. There's a great kitchen and leisure space for the EMTs and firefighters, with seminar-type rooms for discussions and more training.
The Raquette Lake Fire Department is 75 miles away from the nearest hospital. There's Glen's Falls. There's a hospital in Utica. There is a small hospital in Saranac Lake. And there's a longer haul down to Albany.
The men and women volunteers at the Raquette Lake Fire Department will be the first on the scene, and will remain with a patient for several hours. They might treat someone experiencing a cardiac event, a slip-and-fall in the home, a car accident, or a ski accident.
The ribbon-cutting ceremony at the regionally significant facility in Raquette Lake was attended by me, my team, and Champy.
Such a major event for a huge chunk of the Adirondack Park. Where was Elise?
**We 're already winning**
Back to the discussion I started with - canvassing is going well. Other than fundraising (which is still really horrible) the campaign is going really well.
You may have heard me say that we have three ways to win: 1) we get more than 50% of the vote (a long shot, but not impossible); 2) we build our processes and networks so that we are better prepared for the midterm elections; 3) we may not turn NY-21 blue, but we can darn sure turn it pink or purple.
In that sense, we are already winning. I had a very brief conversation with Jamie Raskin about two weeks ago. He asked about polling. I responded, "There is no polling for NY-21, Jamie." He was dumbfounded. "Surely the DNC has numbers," said he. Well, if they have numbers, they haven't shared them with me.
This exchange was just one more example of how the races in the large rural districts are completely different from the races in the urban centers. I'm not even sure they know how to run a race in a large rural district.
But honestly, I think we are on to something here. We've got record numbers of registered Republicans telling us that they are planning to vote blue this time. Some of them already have, on absentee ballots.
It's too early to really tell, and there really are no polls here in upstate New York, but it seems to me that we're already winning. At a bare minimum, we are turning NY-21 pink, and maybe even purple! And maybe -- just maybe -- we can turn it blue!
We can do a lot more "winning" in the next 23 days! Keep up the good work.

clean_body: Notes about Canvassing, NY Prop 1, and The Raquette Lake Fire Department | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more NY-21 Updates on the Congressional Race Notes about Canvassing, NY Prop 1, and The Raquette Lake Fire Department | | | Oct 14 | | | | | | | | | | | | Knock Knock - Reports from Canvassing In New York 21, I'm happy to report that there is a silent majority of voters who seem to have a plan to vote blue this November. My polling is not scientific. It is not tested. It is not statistically measured for accuracy. My polling is based on dropping in on three different random blocks in three different cities, each chosen for the convenience en route to another destination. In Massena (St. Lawrence County), we picked a block that appeared to be populated by the working poor. I'm basing this on the condition of the homes. It was a block that had a mixture of manufactured homes, apartments, duplexes, and single-family homes. All of them seemed like the last stop before doubling up with a cousin or being out on the street. Again - this wasn't scientific data-gathering. This is purely anecdotal. Out of 28 homes, we met someone just waking up at noon from an all-night shift at a hospital. She was cool, really glad that someone from my campaign stopped by, and apologetic that we were seeing her in jammies and before her cup of morning coffee. We met 5 stay-at-home moms. A few were supporters. Another said she was not registered to vote; they were "thinking" about it,. One person angrily said she couldn't see the point of voting. Curiously, for a Friday morning when school should be in session, we saw a number of kids riding bicycles or playing in the yards. (The Special Education teacher in me wanted to ask why they weren't in school, but I refrained.) We met 2 people as they were walking their dogs. We met one guy who seemed to emerge from a cave, shocked that anybody was knocking on his door. He said he was not a voter. I met someone who had an Elise Stefanik sign in her garage that she just had not put out. She said she was thinking. We chatted. I have no idea if I persuaded her or not. In Malone (Franklin County), we picked a street that seemed a little more stable socio-economically, based on the condition of the homes, all of which were single-family residences. (Maybe I'm wrong and they are just a lot deeper in debt than the Massena neighborhood.) Mostly we had positive reactions. "Oh yeah -- ya got my vote!" We met a veteran who was also a retired law enforcement officer. He was angry. His wife had lost 6 cousins in the hurricane North Carolina, and he wanted to know why we were supporting migrants crossing the border illegally, instead of helping our own American citizens. I took a deep breath, and quietly said that I'm sure in his professional experience, he knew a lot about government budgets. There just wasn't any easy way to divert millions of dollars from one line item in the budget to another. I reminded him that Trump had done it; Biden had not. He calmed down. My staffer said, "I see your thin blue line flag. He said yes. We talked about how police officers had been beaten on January 6 and my opponent defends those who participated in the attack. I said bluntly: "She doesn't back the police. She backs Trump." He nodded, looked down, and said, "Yeah." Later I saw him in the neighborhood walking his dog. We smiled and were friendly. Maybe I had a little bit of influence? Hard to say. Honestly, most of the doors we knocked on in Malone were really glad to see us, and they proudly assured us that I had their vote. In Plattsburgh (Clinton County) we picked a block that seemed to have upper-middle-class homes. Again - appearances only. I did not check the property tax rolls. House after house was positive. "You're running against Elise? Ya got my vote!" We even heard that through a ring camera from someone who wasn't home. Two notable exceptions: a person who was friendly at first, but then when he asked my party affiliation, I lost him. We were still friendly. But the conversation chilled at that point. Another group of three young African American men seemed non-committal. One said he would not vote because he doesn't see the point. The other two weren't sure what their voting plan was. Here's my point: nobody slammed a door in my face. Nobody said, "Get the (bleep) off-a my porch!" Definitely no weapons were wielded. And these were random stops -- no VAN data, no idea who these people were or what their prior voting record might be. I could canvass like this all day every day. One of my favorite aspects of running for office is talking to undecided voters. They keep me alert, and offer me a challenge. Can we talk about the protections against age discrimination in NY Prop 1? NY Proposition 1 "adds certain protections to the State Bill of Rights." "Adds anti-discrimination provisions to State Constitution. Covers ethnicity, national origin, age, disability, and sex, including sexual orientation, gender identity and pregnancy. Also covers reproductive healthcare and autonomy. A "YES" vote puts these protections against discrimination in the New York State Constitution. A "NO" vote leaves these protections out of the State Constitution." The disinformation wars are rampant. The naysayers predict that if NY Prop 1 passes boy children will join girls' sports teams and invade their locker rooms. They will also go to school as one gender and come home having had gender reassignment surgery. I guess they've never gotten a call from the school nurse demanding that their feverish child be picked up immediately. Schools can't even give a kid a Tylenol to keep a fever down, much less perform gender reassignment surgery. The other piece of misinformation from the naysayers is that illegal immigrants will be allowed to vote in our elections. Not true. I'm all for writing any protections possible into the State Constitution. No new law will be made by passing Prop 1. We just want to keep the protections we have. I realize that a lot of the discussion in favor of Prop 1 has centered on reproductive and gender-affirming choice. I really think that for a certain kind of voter we need to focus on the protections against age discrimination. Maybe you have known someone older than 50 who mysteriously experiences out-of-the-blue harassment at work, only to realize that the employer is trying to perhaps encourage them to quit in order to hire someone half as old at half the salary. Or perhaps you've spoken with someone who has actually been downsized or laid off, only to realize they can't even get an interview, much less a job. Prop 1 and its protections against age discrimination are necessary. Yes, we have protections against age discrimination in the Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967. New York has a similar law. But these are really tough cases to prove. Let's codify these protections, so they are less likely to be repealed if we should ever get another MAGA administration. | | ---|---|--- Champy is here. Where is Elise? My team has very cleverly introduced a campaign mascot to our social media presence. In Lake Champlain, there is a Loch Ness sort of legendary creature that dates back to 1609. My team now takes a small Democratic Blue dinosaur with us, and caption a photo with something like, "Champy is here. Where is Elise?" On Saturday week we attended the dedication of the Raquette Lake Fire Department. For starters, it's a gorgeous facility. It will allow the fire department to park state-of-the-art fire trucks (the old facility was too small for modern fire trucks). There is ample space to move around the vehicles so that proper training of new volunteer firefighters can take place. And there is ample space to park ambulances. There's a great kitchen and leisure space for the EMTs and firefighters, with seminar-type rooms for discussions and more training. The Raquette Lake Fire Department is 75 miles away from the nearest hospital. There's Glen's Falls. There's a hospital in Utica. There is a small hospital in Saranac Lake. And there's a longer haul down to Albany. The men and women volunteers at the Raquette Lake Fire Department will be the first on the scene, and will remain with a patient for several hours. They might treat someone experiencing a cardiac event, a slip-and-fall in the home, a car accident, or a ski accident. The ribbon-cutting ceremony at the regionally significant facility in Raquette Lake was attended by me, my team, and Champy. Such a major event for a huge chunk of the Adirondack Park. Where was Elise? We 're already winning** Back to the discussion I started with - canvassing is going well. Other than fundraising (which is still really horrible) the campaign is going really well. You may have heard me say that we have three ways to win: 1) we get more than 50% of the vote (a long shot, but not impossible); 2) we build our processes and networks so that we are better prepared for the midterm elections; 3) we may not turn NY-21 blue, but we can darn sure turn it pink or purple. In that sense, we are already winning. I had a very brief conversation with Jamie Raskin about two weeks ago. He asked about polling. I responded, "There is no polling for NY-21, Jamie." He was dumbfounded. "Surely the DNC has numbers," said he. Well, if they have numbers, they haven't shared them with me. This exchange was just one more example of how the races in the large rural districts are completely different from the races in the urban centers. I'm not even sure they know how to run a race in a large rural district. But honestly, I think we are on to something here. We've got record numbers of registered Republicans telling us that they are planning to vote blue this time. Some of them already have, on absentee ballots. It's too early to really tell, and there really are no polls here in upstate New York, but it seems to me that we're already winning. At a bare minimum, we are turning NY-21 pink, and maybe even purple! And maybe -- just maybe -- we can turn it blue! We can do a lot more "winning" in the next 23 days! Keep up the good work. If we haven 't met yet, I am Paula Collins, the Democratic and Working Families Party Candidate for New York's 21st Congressional District. Your comments are invaluable to me. Please let me hear from you. Remember that you can always visit my website at www.paulacollinsforcongress.com or by sending me a text at 315-230-3920. | | | | | | | (C) 2024 Paula Collins 548 Market Street PMB 72296, San Francisco, CA 94104 ? ?

We're on the ground rebuilding lives destroyed by
Hurricane Helene. Join our fight!
http://paracom.paramountcommunication.com/p/oWLqF9aWN6

Friend,

The storm is over, but the effects of Hurricane Helene are
still wreaking havoc on thousands of lives. Operation Helo is
pivoting to meet the ongoing needs of the people in Western North
Carolina.

The need for helicopter operations has ceased, but the
challenges for survivors are far from over.

Our mission has now shifted to providing housing assistance,
funeral support, and addressing any forthcoming needs as families
work to rebuild their lives from the devastation.

Your continued support is critical in this new phase. Many
survivors are facing the unimaginable-lost loved ones, destroyed
homes, and uncertain futures.

Operation Helo is here to help ease their burden, but we can't
do it without you.

Your donation today will help:

Provide temporary housing for families who have lost their
homes

Offer funeral assistance to those who tragically lost loved
ones

Support long-term recovery efforts for the hardest-hit
communities

These efforts are essential in helping families take the next
step toward healing and recovery. Every contribution makes a
difference in rebuilding lives after this catastrophic event.

Please consider donating today to help us provide the support
these families desperately need.

Thank you for your compassion and for standing with the people
of North Carolina in their time of need.

| | | | Hi folks, Jon Tester and Sherrod Brown here. We’re reaching out today because we’re in the middle of the two most competitive Senate campaigns in the country, and we need your help to win. We’re not the typical politicians you’d expect to see every day in the Senate. One of us is a seven-fingered dirt farmer. The other has been called disheveled, wrinkled, and rumpled. Neither of us are winning any best dressed awards anytime soon. **But the thing that really sets us apart? We’ll work with anyone to get the job done for our constituents.** And we’ll always stand up to the special interests in Washington to help folks back home. But right now, we’re in the toughest reelection fight of our lives. **FIRST,** election experts called us the most vulnerable Democratic senators up in 2024. **THEN,** Mitch McConnell and his cronies said they would spend over a hundred million dollars to try to defeat us. **NOW,** we’re officially up against two self-funding multimillionaires who are bankrolling their campaigns themselves. We can’t write our campaigns million dollar checks. But we’ve got something better: You. Our supporters are teachers, electricians, farmers, autoworkers, you name it — who work hard every day to make a living and together, we can make a difference. [**_Things are really heating up in our races so we’ve set a rapid response Big Sky Buckeye Fund goal to raise $500,000 in the next 48 hours to fight back against the millions being thrown our way. So we’re asking: Will you chip in $10 to split between our campaigns and No Dem Left Behind to keep a seven-fingered dirt farmer and a disheveled champion for the Dignity of Work in the Senate?_**](https://click.nodemleftbehind.com/click/gpnv-2v2avu-ffcqp8-kyd76rh9/)

**Good Morning**! On this day in in 1947, Capt. Chuck Yeager became the first person to break the sound barrier in the XS-1 research jet, launched from the bomb bay of a B-29. ([See Video](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0j71qwzAYAJ9G2mKkT3_2oKHQeinp0pKORj-fYwU5Co5sk7cv6Z71Dg7u9zgcXcrpev5yM9o6lsGFmjYcODtweQA5SBrtiAgoKFpuoO2Y0lzQyToxtp1XqLVAA0z5IJQKKnY6eBOjockCA8kZl5yxVsomeh06jcp4DUG1nEiGMdWyNJeSrnXCMT_KhksTykyznWq93Yl4I9AT6Pd9bx5lravHp38SV8NERL8R8T5dTj9u9afvzw-62HjbU87prg2R7Dy7lP-T9cXhZuEvAAD__ylkUp8))We've seen plenty of rain these past few weeks, but here's something new: A rare deluge flooded parts of the Sahara Desert for the first time in decades. [The photos ](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0j7FuwyAQQL8GNlvH5bDxwNDFW7p2tDCcYypsIkCx-vdVund70hue3td9ubuY4vn4dAfbtuXF-RZfvCjoFHVIC8lgN2bkm2SrRjQT6EHd5G4JABSvCtzEbCZjtOHREGi9ugBKy2gRkBQoUgCGqA_r4KeB9bgO6LVRgoBDbLn03zmebect_eQXl97nQya7t_as4vYhcBY4X9fV-7WefNW3Fzi_UeBc3e6K6wJXLq3bUs4hno_uyCV7nwXOstjwvGJKsQ6jIHgcLqa_Rvtn-WXxNwAA__-T4Fi5)are worth seeing. Today's sponsor is [Shared Hope International](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0z7FuhSAUgOGngU3DOSByB4YubrdrR4NyEBq8GCA2ffum3bv-w598H8_16VJOr-PdnWR7KKvbe7ppBTGAGlCtinsbiJAkJwszmoeYNEge7SblQwYR5OxCMNrrHaQxCiZPAc0MPFkUqECAAiGMUqPf9P7QNM2bxn0ywJQgn3qp42dJrx4p5O9yUx33cvJsY-9XY_KN4cJwadFV8rFcNJZ6MFzcdZHLodSzMVwqtV4qDT3SkNNNv41X66-vlHNqemZKHKdL-W_e_7HeFn8CAAD__4a4Vq0), an organization dedicated to rescuing children from being enslaved, trafficked, and sold every day. ## Armed Man Arrested Near Trump Rally
A Nevada man identified as [Vem Miller was arrested at a checkpoint](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0z7FugzAQgOGnsbcg-zgbe_DQhS1dOyJsjuQiAylYQPL0Vbt3_qVf-r6u3bXnzPPts58olHHp-lR4p06ri8YLYIdyCCMRUC0p6AacV8bqWt6Ddr2PqvYmAfgmYrIW6tE503gYyZDkAApQK41aKYdYDdEmb8k00UIyTgtUNHBZ1uqx8FzuNObXstNapWWSOdxLeW6i_hDQCmiP46hiTL9NQDvTsQloM-8koE35tZ_n-_34Potcw_A8OGfebCNQ3aae89-x_APcA_wEAAD__20yUl0) about a quarter-mile from Donald Trump's rally in Coachella, California, on Saturday, after being found in possession of firearms, including a shotgun, a loaded handgun, and a high-capacity magazine.Police also discovered multiple passports, driver's licenses under different names, a fake license plate, as well as [fake VIP and press passes to the rally](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0ULGupDAQ-5rQZZUMIbBFimvo9tor0UCGTU6BoGR2EX9_4vrXWJYt2Zb_vKYXxhT392_cyPGaJ1w4fmnSSmojwUym8W4lAmobcrqH4ak6q9smOG36Fgc7t72280KWrFV92yug7glAvokOFBittNFKDcY8_GyXp6Wuny0s3aCFUeQj5_L4m-POgdZ05S-Vx5K3JrnAfFTR_hIwChj368iVb0vAeAcLGLW6oRUwfqrc6awCRg6xeMnlsx0Sa8Va444c8y6RmbaDJYcTC5OXZ6BdYtnIyw1vVqjeev5wjZ7kknEJlBLKgildsgYqcV1lxetuaorzxxlTitX2wqj3hjH9384_XPl18C8AAP__ShJ3zw).Authorities confirmed the incident [did not impact Trump's safety](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0kLGupCAUQL8GOwwXL6gFxTZ2s81ks6VBuSpvEAwyY-bvX-b1rz7FOTn_b-PN-uDj-tfuZMqSRjsX_6IRBAfkEkesnFmIJDUVGWhl1wuloak2o6EDhU5NQD11DTpl1SQsLr3rWo1QeSOFRBCAIESHWLtJz70m1U5azqoDhoKcLynXX8nHstES3ulFuZ7TXgWzlXKcrPnD5MDkYKc50nXWa_pgJod_dyaHy2e6l5TfTA67jTwk68jx9Rm5zZnOQo7PG82P42PgLkUbHC_5uR8nv4geFB0HwFYrCX2VjTsuH4I_dctQrLv14aem_DLnZeR3AAAA__-UVGcC) or the rally attendees.Miller was released on $5,000 bail and is scheduled to appear in court on January 2, 2025._" We probably stopped another assassination attempt,"_ Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco said.
## Advanced U.S. Defense System Heads to Israel
The Pentagon announced Sunday that the U.S. will send an [advanced missile defense system to Israel](http://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJx0kL1u7CAQRp8Gd6xgAP8UFLdxt7dNaWEY1hNhsAxy5LePNkqb-tN3dHQ-nsvTUaL8-u92tC2WxflGFy5ScKk56EV3wUZEQNWhlQOMkzC9VN1mvVF6kMobgTH4wcR1HRA8mIjKuWnqyIIALYXUUohR60dYez_1aIa1B29GybTAQK2cj89CuW0Y010uPB--7F2yW2tHZeofg5nB3DbcKKX3xmA-SiJ_M5gDRswVGcx6UmIae35gbu5VMv-ilHjFHLgLl8seA9-pVkrIf1-83rXhzndK1Nx58wPPWnLGxFvhVE-HicHcnTYcbxrVfmBavHZHPyJd-6PZZeE7AAD__4DZcTw), along with the military personnel to operate it.The move to provide direct U.S. assistance in defending Israel follows a [missile attack by Iran on Oct. ## Foster Care Ruling Overturned
A federal appeals court removed U.S. District Judge Janis Jack from a lawsuit involving Texas' foster care system and [overturned her previous judgment](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kLGOszAQhJ_GdEa2s0AoXPwNXf4mOl2JFnshPhmMzAaStz-R_srRjGZG3_etv2GIYZn-40yWX2Pq0XHYqddKapAGeii8HZRvdUFWN-baqqs2UDxsjb5FdFjXIymgBgbnq_oCeqjbqvFDEaxRBrTSoFV1NaYkp8ER0jA2aDR5AYp84JRLfhDTC7cxvtNOuXRpLqJ9MK-buPwTphOmw8EtdGzllE5bmO7rLkx3hEx3Tvl9JtaVMG7SpWdmeRbxMy-nXpjmleUYFh-WSWaa006b_Hn6ieRnWWoNDbRtpYps_XqEGMNWNwLUNGOIn0f8F6Hdmt8AAAD___kta7E) against the state. In an April ruling, Jack imposed a $100,000-per-day fine against Texas for failing to resolve outstanding abuse and neglect claims. The 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals determined that Jack's ruling [exceeded constitutional limits](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kL9utDAQxJ_GdIvs_fzxp3BxRegubZQKLbC-c4Ltk23g8vYR16eakean0Wg-ruOV3OrC7Z08m_K0caS5uJ1HJUFpQD3qajGTXHpVsVEtdr3sFOrqbtRMDbU9dxNP3EndNkiIvWarsGPbVM6gRK2k0kr-7xBrnpWemXiyLaHiRWjJiysx1eXOhZ-U7foTd071HH21mnspjyz-XQQOAofjOGqfw5kJHDjAlgUOgY9TXn6OWyqQ2MedM3xty43Bpujh1Q025sIJZkoMKx15cye8c8qcwbt1dTFkcAGsC3ziCXKhwgIHSnC5qEzfn29VMsvjOOnctELLmye3vgaXvw7cDf4GAAD__6tGdyA) and criticized her for blatant bias against Texas and its attorneys. The Friday decision is the latest in a lawsuit that has been [ongoing since 2011](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kLGO2zAQRL-G6tYg15RkFSrSqLu0KY0Vd2nToU2BXFuXvw_OSXvlzAAPmPfr4_xBKafH5SfdZdbPWM4UNL3k7Cw4D-jPvuN5tTy5TmY34mmyJ4e-u87i4tAPTDQFXocQR-4RicejdThZ5i7NaNE767yz_QnxIMH5ICRrHAmdsPFWOGmpB72Kyie1mP-Ul9RDKPcuz1fVrZnjD4OLwWXf98Meib5GgwtVTSGLweUhezO4NCX9im8Q_C9jinqFkGp4JoVQnlWBtk0oN6jyktqkwe3JF4EbPVKDG4XfEMpD5b4plMpS4R8xlqZSIVAVyLS3Z1KDC55GGI5oA1EPkYOAt9bDynwETxwmWnnqB9fVmbc95ZzaMBpvL3dK-f1Tv_P-mvFvAAAA__-dUoiv), when advocates sought to address inadequacies within the state's foster care system.
## SpaceX Conducts Historic Starship Test
SpaceX completed a [historic test flight](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kK1y8zAQAJ9GYvLoLop_gMBHzPLRQs9ZOseaUWKPdLWTt--0oKxswc6C_bhNN0o5Pe__6cFeXss2UZB08ATWgDPoJqejn20cQLOHDvvB9oBOrz4ih2tPQ7w4bOfQW4J5iK0FsANeulYnjxYdWHBgrz1iwwFcYOJ56QiBo3KWY5KtNLKy8Ivqkt_bwaUJ20Nnv4rsVV3-KRwVjud5NgflzO_ATymUvy2FY90p8OsXzF54p8LVLFsxSapZ0iKrqUKlrmk3mT6fYVU46uLjfqacU2075ez9QeknquWvFYfHrwAAAP__-jJjmA) of its massive reusable Starship rocket Sunday morning, the day after receiving federal approval for the launch. The 400-foot rocket launched from the company's Boca Chica facility at 7:25 a.m. Seven minutes after liftoff, giant "chopsticks" mechanical arms [caught the first-stage Super Heavy booster](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kLFuwyAQQL8Gb1hwIbE9MHTxlq4dLTjOAZUECy6x-_dVund70hue9L6uy9WlnB63T3cny8daFoecXrRoJbWRYBbTBetVmHRHVg8wTmrUYLpoYTRrCCp47RWiPyGdL4MGNylvjBt8lywoMFppo9V5BOgJtUFy5NfBgaYgjKKQuNSeIzEdrq35p7yo9ljuXbaReWvi9CFgFjDv-95jrOXxtgJmfGZ-VhIwu8oJ85va5pAO2djVFtMms3s-MEpfSmOqshb8JpZ6Gk_mDJd-i1tXbdj2lHNql0EYdbu7lP_6_N-Pl4XfAAAA__9R8mTt) on the launch pad, a first for the company and a major step toward its goal of reusability. Meanwhile, the stainless steel Starship spacecraft [splashed down in the Indian Ocean](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0j7Fq7DAQRb9G6mw0Y3klFyoePAwpNm1KI0vj1YC8Npay3vx92EDKlJd74HA-rtPVc-b77d2v5Opz2SYfKj9oAtWAblBPWkY3qziAJAcG7aAsoJbJGQi9BjNjNJduUHawZsDZWLr0iwkqSHaoUIMCDaq3iC0F0IE8zYvxCBSFVhS5bkdbE1V6-rLkr-1BRxu2VWaXat2L6P4JHAWO53m2ZfeBnq9b4Jj95z0kKgLHlUvh7f4Cu9_xFkX3v1R_lMR7s2S-pdr08nBxPzlnLhcjtLqtnvOPr_7V_3D4HQAA___3SF4Z) without incident. The rocket had exploded or experienced mechanical issues during the previous test flights.
## El Paso To Try Variable Speed Limit
El Paso will become the first city in Texas to [implement a variable speed limit](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kDFv8yAUAH8NbFjwghMYGL7FW761owXmkaCCscyTnfbXV83e-aQ76T7u893nktfHf1_R0Su12S-UD5yVFEoL0LPm0QUZreLo1A2MlUaB5k8XAC7j1ZjFGJTBpuitxcs4WmkCypR4diBBK6m0kqMBGHBRekGPId08KIxMS4yZ2j7QEwlfvqfy1Q7ch6VVXtyTaOvs8o_BxGA6z3P4pF5_IYNpxbMzmLCIzfcmqIlct4IVVxJvl1CdxOH37ENB0TfEKL7bigwmvru4nbmU3K83puWj-lzeUfprwuHgJwAA__-h1mEA) on Wednesday when dynamic speed limit signs will be activated on a 2-mile stretch of U.S. 54 southbound north of I-10, where the standard speed limit is 60 mph. The new system aims to reduce speeding by [lowering the speed limit](http://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJx0kbGS2zAMRL9G6uAhadqyChVp3F3alB6QgCwkFKkhYZ3u7zNx6it3dot98359PD5QkuTnT1x50mMuD4wqOz-sAevB-YfvaQqGRtvzZAd3G83NOt8v08XF8WboPF4G9HwlGsZwHa_DOczjOVrTy-SM89ZYb83l5tyJo_WRkcM8oLNMnTdMoqWedGHlA9ucvsrO9RTL2qdpUd1ad_7RuXvn7n_mcuj-r-rcPfNn69w9lYjpfwSk36-mGBJD25gJkqyi0OSZG2iBwCC5KabEBCXDq108SAZOsGEr8D4AeoAeVBSIN6y6clYoM2jF3LZSFVVKhlixLUCMukCoQk9-jxYGXLlKxAbbi7MyJAmVIWJrQl9QC1JfJ9o-JSVp16Hz5rmipDexfmdgn9zfAAAA__-EhpAU)--either automatically or manually--up to 10 mph based on traffic or weather conditions. In 2023, El Paso saw 3,855 speed-related crashes, resulting in 30 deaths and 65 serious injuries.

subject: Disabled Marine’s Wife Loses Baby After FBI Raid
body:
Captain Christopher Kuehne, US Marine Corps (retired) is a disabled combat veteran and a patriot. He rose from Private to Captain and was decorated twice for valor in combat.

[](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zqq3f034c4pjfdgdhv8jsqe4cqk9kokdnp47gs50_rp22sh2s8i6eoj0sji61ob2cph2bs)

**[Please give a crucial $25, $50, $100, or more right now to help free January 6 peaceful protesters!](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zbq4hat5qdii7lhdjofl3jgkj6uhr6hupjkd24g0_rp22sh2s8i6eoj0sji61ob2cph2bs)**

Captain Christopher Kuehne, US Marine Corps (retired) is a disabled combat veteran and a patriot.

He rose from Private to Captain, and was decorated twice for valor in combat. On his last deployment, a suicide bomber detonated his vest near him. It caused him terrible, permanent injuries resulting in a 100% disability rating.

Christopher is the kind of man you want as your next door neighbor. Or representing you in city hall or on Capitol Hill.

He went to Washington, DC on January 6, 2021 to protect peaceful protesters from being violently attacked by Antifa and Black Lives Matter thugs.

When he peacefully entered the US Capitol building, he attacked no one. He broke nothing.

You know what he did?

**Christopher picked up trash and tried to help the US Capitol Police. Earlier that day, he tried to save the life of a man who needed CPR.**

He then went back home to his wife, Annette, their little boy, Chris, and their unborn baby.

The US flag and Marine Corps flag flew out front, and a sign by the front door said "God Bless America."

It was the dead of winter in Kansas.

**And in the early morning on February 11, 2021, the FBI raided his home. They pointed their rifles at Annette and their little boy. They forced Annette to stand outside in 14-degree weather, barefoot, wearing only a tee shirt and shorts. The next day, she lost the baby.**

(Now Christopher doesn't blame the FBI for his child's death ... but I do.)

He was bulldozed by Joe Biden's corrupt Department of Justice, and forced to plead guilty to a felony he didn't commit, impeding law enforcement during a civil disorder ... or face serious jail time for multiple criminal charges.

**Christopher is serving 75 days in federal prison in San Diego right now. And I bet he isn 't getting all the medical care he needs for his traumatic brain injury and other serious injuries he suffered while serving our country.**

You and I know Christopher is one of many January 6 peaceful protesters who committed no crime. But they've been cruelly hunted, hounded, and harassed by the FBI and DOJ anyway.

Many more still face trial and long prison sentences, far from their families and friends.

Let me tell you, what's being done to Christopher and other innocent Americans is an outrage!

**But there 's something you can do about it.**

I'm Larry Klayman, founder and general counsel for Freedom Watch.

I'm a former federal prosecutor and trial lawyer who's fought for the American people for 47 years.

You've probably seen me on cable news or heard me on talk radio.

**I 'm the only lawyer in American history to have a court rule that a sitting President had committed a crime. I _guarantee_ Bill Clinton still remembers me!**

And I successfully represented the victims of other Clinton scandals, like Filegate, Travelgate, IRS Gate, Chinagate, and many others.

I know what it takes to take on federal agencies, politicians, even presidents, and win. And my critical new lawsuit is a game changer.

**Attorney General Merrick Garland, FBI Director Christopher Wray, their departments and agencies at the U.S. Department of Justice BROKE THE LAW and ILLEGALLY SPIED ON LAW-ABIDING AMERICAN CITIZENS ... and I can PROVE it in court! That means their criminal convictions can be THROWN OUT. And their criminal trials can be THROWN OUT.**

And I'm taking other hard-hitting legal actions to protect our fellow Americans and our endangered rights and freedoms.

Let me tell you, no other legal group in the country is doing what Freedom Watch is doing to defend and free January 6 patriots.

You see, many defense lawyers are scared spitless of the FBI and DOJ. So they tell their clients to plead guilty to crimes they didn't commit ... and they end up in prison.

But Freedom Watch fights!

**[Patriot, please help me get justice for the battered and abused January 6 peaceful protesters and set them free with your critically important gift of at least $25, $50, $100 or more immediately.](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2z9ci5r13f335pscmrj8r7ulvk463c0aboibgu318_rp22sh2s8i6eoj0sji61ob2cph2bs)**

I'm counting on you.

Thank you for doing whatever you can **now**.

In Justice,

Larry Klayman
Founder, Judicial Watch and Freedom Watch
Chairman and General Counsel, Freedom Watch, Inc.

**P.S. Patriot, Christopher 's wife, Annette, lost their baby the day after the FBI raided their home. Now he's in prison for a crime he didn't commit. **This madness must end. It's time to free the January 6 peaceful protesters and send them home to their families.

**[Please give what you can immediately to help Freedom Watch fight for them in court. $25, $50, $100, even more...whatever you can spare at this very moment. Every dollar counts.](https://e.youramerica.news/rd/9z2zlavt5gtfjko8k2tttb2ap9l6ajrfsv3ptu4k91o_rp22sh2s8i6eoj0sji61ob2cph2bs)** Thank you so much!

## Do you think that most Americans understand how the Electoral College works and its role in preserving free and representative government?
[YES](https://e.firstlook.news/rd/9z2z19lrpe2m5c05enj2tdnirfsa36ffiu7d9nk8k70_rp22sh2s8i6eoj0sji61p76c9h2bs) [NO](https://e.firstlook.news/rd/9z2zlg6vojimjb4sh8eupjbb8j4i6sp63nbrmpdi27g_rp22sh2s8i6eoj0sji61p76c9h2bs) Dear Fellow American, I am enclosing a survey on a very urgent matter. It will only take a moment of your time, but the topic is vital to our nation's future. A movement is growing, led by progressives--but supported by many well-meaning Americans--to change the way we elect our president. In effect, it seeks to do away with the Electoral College as devised by the Framers of our Constitution. That's why Hillsdale College is conducting a **National Survey on Presidential Selection.** By completing this survey and returning it to me as soon as possible, you will help Hillsdale College more clearly understand the views of mainstream Americans concerning this issue--views we will make available to policymakers and opinion leaders. You can complete the **National Survey on Presidential Selection **by using the link below: **[https://lp.hillsdale.edu/electoral-college-survey](https://e.firstlook.news/rd/9z2z6h3ehkepkpark5vi1ibt71c9qf1en86ct2fkpvo_rp22sh2s8i6eoj0sji61p76c9h2bs)** Please represent your state and take the **National Survey on Presidential Selection today**. Thank you for your time and attention--and for your friendship and support of liberty. Warm regards, Larry P. Arnn President, Hillsdale College Pursuing Truth and Defending Liberty Since 1844

A couple of weekends ago, I was up in NorCal for a wedding, so I went to see my law school roommate, [Ryan](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ba9ec4e4-7b91-4615-b041-9a267ca1586e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), who got his P.h.D. and is now a pastor and theologian at the Bay Church in Concord, CA. It was my first time publicly reflecting on the campaign and what I learned. I really enjoyed it.
You can watch the full episode [here](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/6773234c-6e07-4ce4-8ae8-98525d6eee49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).

And if you're inclined to support the mission of the Bay Church, [you can do so here.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/4f8c73cd-ea8b-453b-ae99-0d8cd4c13b97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The next few weeks in the United States are likely to be chaotic, and we all have to take care of ourselves, even as we stay engaged.
Hope this helps.
_-- pai_

name: Ruben Gallego
subject: some things you never get used to
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
I don’t know if I’ll ever get used to watching a former president attack me personally. I grew up with next to nothing and one of the most powerful people in the world just calls me out at his rallies.
#

Peter, it’s Ruben.
I don’t know if I’ll ever get used to watching a former president come after me personally. I grew up with next to nothing and one of the most powerful people in the world just calls me out at his rallies.
That’s always going to be weird to me.
But that’s what Donald Trump did when he came here in August. Again in September. On social media earlier this week. And again, last night, in Arizona.
He came back because Arizona is critical to his chances this year, and winning this state is personal for him after we beat him back in 2020.
He knows if he can help defeat me he’s got an open path to the White House. He’s got to go through us to win.
That raises the stakes of our campaign beyond just one seat in the U.S. Senate, and beyond our Senate Majority. This race is about beating Trump, once and for all.
I need you with me to do it, Peter.

He knows if he can help defeat me he’s got an open path to the White House. He’s got to go through us to win. subject: Common sense facts
body:
Peter, It’s that time again. Every four years we get inundated with mail, texts, and emails about the presidential election.
|
---
| Peter, It’s that time again. Every four years we get inundated with mail, texts, and emails about the presidential election. Everywhere you turn there’s another news story, post, or video. With all this constant information, you think it’d be easy to get all the facts. But, unfortunately, that’s not the case. The mainstream media has chosen their side. They shill for the Left constantly–from glowing, softball interviews, to running interference during debates. They tell us everything is going great under the Biden-Harris administration. But our daily experience tells us otherwise. **So, where can you turn to get the Common Sense facts?** That’s where you come in. The Common Sense Club and its members have a duty to start speaking up–even when what we say isn’t politically correct. And we need to speak up especially when our message contradicts the consensus in the media. I talked a little about this in this video →

#

We're going to be blunt, team:
**_We are way behind on our fundraising goals for this month._**
Sorry to be so direct, but we needed to let you know the truth.
This is not the time for us to fall short. In just two days, we’re facing the October 16th pre-general election FEC deadline. This will be our **final** FEC filing deadline before Election Day. Once this deadline passes, we’ll be required to report both the amount we’ve raised and the number of individual donations we’ve received in the first half of this month.
With where we stand right now, we don’t have the numbers to have a strong showing on this report. That’s why today, we’re launching an urgent FEC fundraising drive with a big goal to raise $50,000 online by Wednesday at midnight.

We can’t let the gun lobby think that there is room for them to swoop in at the last minute and launch attacks against our endorsed gun safety candidates.
**_But a weak FEC report will signal to them that they can do just that._**
With just 22 days left until Election Day, we cannot afford to slow down in our fundraising. Your donation right now is more important than it’s ever been because it will be invested right into races that need our help to fight back against hate-fueled gun lobby attacks.

Hey there,
In October 2021, I had been an employee of Kellogg’s for almost 18 years.
I had dropped out of college and gone to work for the company after my wife got pregnant. Life’s easy when all you gotta do is take care of yourself – but we had diapers to buy and needed health insurance for our growing family.
When I applied in 2004, there were 6 positions and 600 applications. Working at Kellogg’s promised to be a lifelong career. A good-paying job that afforded me the opportunity to become a homeowner, let my wife stay home with the kids, live decently, retire some day, and hopefully live happily ever after.
But over the years, wages became a two-tier system. New workers were being paid less than workers had made decades earlier. Cost of living adjustments weren’t keeping up anywhere near inflation. Retirement and health insurance plans had been gutted. It just wasn’t right. They were making record profits – and doing it off the backs of workers.
**So in October 2021, we walked out. And as president of our local union, I led the strike.**
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/94981600/505199687/92586991?refcode=em20241014am2-nd&amounts=5%2C10%2C25%2C35%2C50%2C100%2C250&refcode2=b5e84b9a-348a-ef11-8474-6045bda8aae9&recurring=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjIxNiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiNWU4NGI5YS0zNDhhLWVmMTEtODQ3NC02MDQ1YmRhOGFhZTkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1G7vm96m3g6gFUOTJ2qhCnumkFtF7D3oNprcFM21zO4=)
It was the first time many of us had ever walked a picket line. It was cold, but we were determined to hold our lines even through the dead of the winter if we had to. Every worker knew we were a part of something bigger than ourselves. We were in a fight for the future of the American middle class.
After 11 weeks, and the company threatening to permanently replace every union worker, we reached an agreement. More importantly, we saved 500 good-paying jobs here in Nebraska alone.
It was one of the proudest moments of my life.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/94981601/505199688/92586991?refcode=em20241014am2-nd&amounts=5%2C10%2C25%2C35%2C50%2C100%2C250&refcode2=b5e84b9a-348a-ef11-8474-6045bda8aae9&recurring=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjIxNiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiNWU4NGI5YS0zNDhhLWVmMTEtODQ3NC02MDQ1YmRhOGFhZTkiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=1G7vm96m3g6gFUOTJ2qhCnumkFtF7D3oNprcFM21zO4=)
Following the strike, I was fired. The company has its version of events for why, but I believe it was because I was union president. Someone had to pay – and my head was on the chopping block.
It’s easy to let yourself get beaten down by life. To let big corporations and the politicians they own in Washington make all the decisions – and just accept that that’s how things will always be. But that’s not me.
**Instead, I’ve decided to run against one of the most corporate politicians – U.S. Senator Republican Deb Fischer – and with your help, we are going to defeat her.**
Four brand-new polls now show me narrowly LEADING Republican Deb Fischer, and according to experts at FiveThirtyEight, Nebraska is now the CLOSEST Senate race in the entire country.
**I am taking on Republican Senator Deb Fischer just like I took on Kellogg’s. But I sure as hell am not taking money from corporate PACs, so I need grassroots donors like you to give now if we’re going to win this Senate seat.**

body:
Peter,

With just 21 days left until Election Day, our team is gearing up for one final push.

Our grassroots movement has helped keep Minnesota blue for years, but this election is the biggest challenge we’ve ever faced. Polling indicates that Donald Trump and Kamala Harris are neck-and-neck, and Real Clear Politics recently downgraded Minnesota from “Leans Democrat” to “Toss Up.”

With reproductive and civil freedoms, voting rights, and so much more on the line, we can’t afford to come up short. Our team needs to reach as many voters as possible, and there’s no time to waste.

We’re committed to mobilizing Democratic voters and connecting with people in hard-to-reach communities, but we can’t do this important work without support from people like you.

Our records show that you’re still eligible for Minnesota’s Political Contribution Refund (PCR) program, which means you can donate $75 (or $150 for couples) to our campaign and receive a full refund from the state of Minnesota.

Peter, will you make a refundable $75 donation right now to help us reach as many Minnesotans as possible before Election Day?

Donald Trump’s disrespect of Americans with disabilities has no limit. He told wealthy donors that Kamala Harris was “retarded,” told his own family members that a relative with a disability “should just die,” and viciously mocked a reporter’s disability to a jeering crowd of thousands. As founder of Able Dems, this fight is personal. But I never gave up - and today, I’m asking you to fight alongside me to defeat MAGA Republicans. We won’t let them throw us off of healthcare, gut Social Security and Medicare, or attack democracy. body:
The climate crisis is real. Our response must be too.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20241014&t=1&akid=1306%2E587540%2EK0bmYh)
Our climate is in crisis, Peter. 🚨
We're stuck with leadership that would rather serve corporate interests than address the existential threat our environment faces. We NEED new blood in the game – young people who will act on our concerns in the places of power where it matters most.
The facts are stark:
🚨2024 is on track to be the hottest year in recorded history.
🚨This summer broke global heat records for the second consecutive year.
🚨We've experienced 12 straight months of global temperatures above pre-industrial levels – a critical threshold for climate change.
Just this month, when we should have had a typical transition from the summer to fall, we instead faced incessant and dangerous heat waves that broke 85 years+ records across the West coast.
🌡️ San Francisco hit 97°F (broke its previous record, set in 1992)
🌡️ San Jose scorched at 103°F (the hottest week ever recorded in the city's history)
🌡️ Santa Rosa matched its 1930 record at a blistering 102°F
🌡️ San Rafael topped the charts at a staggering 107°F (12°F higher than its previous record)
While these numbers are alarming, what's even more concerning is the lack of meaningful action from our current leaders. **We can't afford to wait any longer.**
That is why Leaders We Deserve is committed to electing young leaders who:
✅ Understand the urgency of the climate crisis
✅ Refuse to take corporate money, _especially_ from fossil fuel companies
✅ Will fight for bold climate policies
**[Peter, we need your help to ensure these passionate, climate-focused champions are elected this November. Will you chip in to support their voice?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20241014?refcode=em20241014&amount=5&refcode2=1306_587540_K0bmYh&akid=1306%2E587540%2EK0bmYh)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-20241014?amount=5&refcode=em20241014-1306&refcode2=1306_587540_K0bmYh&akid=1306%2E587540%2EK0bmYh)**
The time for half-measures and empty promises is over. We deserve leaders who will live to see the consequences of today’s decisions and have the moxie to make tough choices for our planet’s future.
Together, we can break the cycle of inaction and build a sustainable future.
Thank you for your support,
Leaders We Deserve

subject: 🚨 The Truth About Measure 4 and Wildfire Relief

body:
